/api/dashboards:
    get:
      description: Returns a paginated list of dashboards. Each result includes title, description, tags, and metadata, but not the full panel layout. Use `GET /api/dashboards/{id}` to retrieve the complete state.
      operationId: get-dashboards
      parameters:
        - description: The page of results to return.
          in: query
          name: page
          required: false
          schema:
            default: 1
            minimum: 1
            type: number
        - description: The number of results to return per page.
          in: query
          name: per_page
          required: false
          schema:
            default: 20
            maximum: 1000
            minimum: 1
            type: number
        - description: Filters results by `title` and `description` using Elasticsearch [`simple_query_string`](https://www.elastic.co/docs/reference/query-languages/query-dsl/query-dsl-simple-query-string-query) syntax. Multi-word terms require all words to match.
          in: query
          name: query
          required: false
          schema:
            type: string
        - description: A tag ID to include. Accepts a single tag ID or multiple tag IDs. When multiple are specified, library items matching any of the tag IDs are included.
          in: query
          name: tags
          required: false
          schema:
            default: []
            description: Tag IDs associated with this dashboard.
            items:
              maxLength: 250
              type: string
            maxItems: 100
            type: array
        - description: A tag ID to exclude. Accepts a single tag ID or multiple tag IDs. When multiple are specified, library items matching any of the tag IDs are excluded.
          in: query
          name: excluded_tags
          required: false
          schema:
            default: []
            description: Tag IDs associated with this dashboard.
            items:
              maxLength: 250
              type: string
            maxItems: 100
            type: array
        - description: A tag name to include. Accepts a single tag name or multiple tag names. When multiple are specified, library items matching any of the tag names are included. If the same name is shared by multiple tags, items matching any of those tags are included.
          in: query
          name: tag_names
          required: false
          schema:
            items:
              type: string
            maxItems: 100
            type: array
            x-state: Generally available; added in 9.6.0
        - description: A tag name to exclude. Accepts a single tag name or multiple tag names. When multiple are specified, library items matching any of the tag names are excluded. If the same name is shared by multiple tags, items matching any of those tags are excluded.
          in: query
          name: excluded_tag_names
          required: false
          schema:
            items:
              type: string
            maxItems: 100
            type: array
            x-state: Generally available; added in 9.6.0

        '200':
          content:
            application/json:

The dashboard and the alert rule both exist in Kibana. The rule has already run once and succeeded with no alerts. I checked through the API that the dashboard saved all 8 panels, but I couldn't open it in a browser, so I haven't seen the charts draw.

**1. What the data holds.** The data view `Kibana Sample Data Logs` uses `timestamp` as its time field. Each document is one web request, with these main fields:
- the response code (`response.keyword`)
- response size (`bytes`)
- the client's IP address (`clientip`)
- the requested URL and the referring page (`url.keyword`, `referer`)
- the client's operating system and browser (`machine.os.keyword`, `agent.keyword`)
- source and destination countries (`geo.src`, `geo.dest`) and map coordinates (`geo.coordinates`)
- other fields: `extension`, `tags`, `memory`, `phpmemory` and `hour_of_day`

**2. Dashboard "EFF-852b091f Web logs overview"** (id `0bacf03f-f57e-40f4-8bde-d19bed765f3b`, default time range is the last 7 days). Its 8 panels are:
- **Top row of single numbers:** total requests, unique visitors (counted by client IP), average response size, and the number of 5xx errors.
- **Requests over time by response code:** a stacked bar chart.
- **Response code distribution:** a pie chart.
- **Requests by OS:** a pie chart.
- **Top requested URLs:** a bar chart of the 10 most requested URLs.

**3. Rule "EFF-852b091f 5xx spike"** (id `4aab5ca5-4bfc-4eb2-b8fb-fa101786a1d7`) is an Elasticsearch query rule on `kibana_sample_data_logs`. It runs every minute, counts requests with a response code from 500 to 599 over the last 5 minutes, and fires when the count is above 10. It has no actions attached, so it will create alerts but won't send any notifications. To get notified, add a connector such as email or Slack.

The 5xx filter compares the codes as text rather than numbers. That gives the right result here because every response code in this data has three digits.
